title: Gimli Glider: fuel believed loaded vs. fuel actually needed (lb)
notes: Air Canada Flight 143, July 23, 1983: ground crew used the wrong fuel-density conversion factor while switching to metric, loading 20,400 lb of fuel instead of the roughly 45,000 lb needed. Both engines flamed out at 41,000 feet; the crew glided the Boeing 767 to a dead-stick landing at a former air base in Gimli, Manitoba. All 69 aboard survived.
